$comment: USPA's competition rules, as far as an attempt planner has to know them,
transcribed from the rulebook cited in `rulebook`.
This file is the toolkit's only copy of these rules. Every surface that answers
a legality question under USPA -- the attempt ladder, the submission countdown,
the third-deadlift change tracker, fourth-attempt eligibility -- reads the
artifact published from here. There is no fallback profile and there must not
be one: a set of numbers no federation stands behind is the set a hurried user
would leave selected.
WHAT IS TRANSCRIBED AND WHAT IS INTERPRETED
Every figure below is stated outright in the rulebook, and `notes` quotes the
sections it came from. Two fields are the exception and are called out here
because a later reader deserves to know they are readings rather than
quotations:
* `forbidsAttemptBelowFailedWeight` is 6.1.1.2's sentence -- 'At no time may a
lifter request an attempt that is less than any attempt previously
unsuccessful' -- turned into a flag. The sentence is unambiguous; the flag
is the shape.
* `formatOverrides` carries only the single-lift bench press, because that is
the only format 6.1.16 names. USPA's international parent extends the same
allowance further, and it is deliberately NOT copied in: this profile
reports USPA's rulebook, and a rule imported from a related organisation
would be presented under the wrong name at an expeditor's table.
HOW THIS WAS VERIFIED, 2026-08-01
1. The rulebook PDF downloaded, digested, and read as text with `pdftotext
-layout`. `rulebook.sha256` is the digest of those exact bytes.
2. Each figure read back against the numbered section it came from, listed
in `provenance.sections`.
3. Cross-read against the corresponding public rule pages of USPA's
international parent, which state the same sequence of section numbers.
Agreement on every figure here. The cross-read is a check, not a source --
where the two could differ, the USPA rulebook wins.
4. Absence checked as well as presence: the rulebook was searched for any
second-attempt or third-squat change allowance, and states none.
THE PDF IS NOT COMMITTED. It carries the federation's logo and nothing here
needs it. `rulebook.sha256` pins the bytes; `check:upstream` re-downloads and
re-digests them on a schedule, so a revision announces itself without the
document being redistributed.
label: USPA

rulebook.$comment: `revision` is the version the document prints on its cover. `sha256` is the digest of the exact bytes read, and is what actually detects a change; the version string is for a person reading a diff.

openerChange.summary: One change to the first attempt of each lift, higher or lower. In the first group of a session, up to five minutes before the start of that lift's first round. In a later group, up to within five attempts of the end of the previous group's last round.

thirdAttemptChanges.$comment: Stated as an absence: the rulebook grants changes in the third round to the deadlift and to a single-lift bench press, and to nothing else. Recorded as an explicit zero rather than by omission so that a screen can say 'this attempt is locked once submitted' rather than falling silent.

formatOverrides.summary: In a single-lift bench press, two changes are permitted in the third round, higher or lower, on the same conditions as the third deadlift.

fourthAttempt.summary: A fourth attempt at a record needs a successful third attempt, a record already standing before the meet began, a third attempt within 20 kilos of that record, and permission from one of the platform's referees or the expeditor.

notes: Openers are declared at weigh-in, in kilograms.
A missed attempt may be repeated, but only in the next round; a lifter never follows themselves at the same weight.
Within a round the bar only rises. It is lowered only to correct a loading error.
Lifters are called in order of the weight requested. Two lifters on the same weight are ordered by lot number, and then by bodyweight.
A record attempt may be a weight that is not a multiple of 2.5 kg. Every other attempt must be.
A fourth attempt is not part of the meet total and does not affect placing, classification, team points or Best Lifter.
